newsitem.title: UK: N. Sea grades steady, Brent paper in backwardation.
newsitem.headline: N. Sea grades steady, Brent paper in backwardation.

text.p: North Sea grades were steady to slightly higher in a quiet market on Friday as the front end of the Brent paper curve headed into backwardation.

No physical Brent deals were reported but a major European refiner picked up a May 25 cargo of Norwegian Statfjord at Dated Brent +22 cents and a second cargo loading May 26-28 was reported to have exchanged hands at the same price.
The buyer of the first cargo was reported to have picked up on Thursday a cargo of Forties at a 25-27 cent premium to Dated Brent and a cargo of Ekofisk at Dated Brent +20 cents.
The loading dates were not available for both deals, reportedly done with a Wall Street trader and which seemed to indicate that the North Sea grades were firmer.
Third decade Forties last traded at Dated Brent +22 cents this week while a May 23 Ekofisk had fetched Dated Brent +16 cents on May 1.
Traders said that two of the Brent cargoes turning wet on Friday were kept, one by Suko and the other by Esso. Koch also kept a cargo but it was not clear if they bought it or got it from the chains.
The fourth cargo got a deferral to May 28-30, the traders added.
On the cash market June Brent rallied in the late afternoon, echoing the morning's bullish mood. The contract was trading 15 cents up at $18.87 a barrel by 1744 GMT, the day's high reached earlier.
Brent intermonth spreads and contracts for differences also firmed in a quiet market.
June/July traded twice at +3 cents after deals at -3 cents in late U.S. trade.
